reviewers.name: Automated Screening Check
reviewers.one_line_take: The file parses cleanly and most required terms are there; communication is the missing one.
reviewers.decision_question: Would this file parse cleanly, and would it come up when a recruiter searches or filters the applicant pool for this job?

reviewers.name: Hiring Manager
reviewers.one_line_take: The survey project and the Excel work earn a call; SQL beyond a class is the open question.
reviewers.decision_question: Based on this resume alone, would I spend 45 minutes interviewing this person for this role?

reviewers.name: Recruiter
reviewers.one_line_take: Clean and easy to skim; the top third says marketing more than analytics.
reviewers.decision_question: In my first fast pass, does this resume go in the 'send to the hiring manager' pile?

reviewers.name: Competing Applicant
reviewers.one_line_take: Your survey project is a real edge, but it is buried and SQL is only listed.
reviewers.decision_question: If this resume sat next to a typical strong applicant's for this job, would it win the interview slot?

reviewers.name: CEO
reviewers.one_line_take: I see useful work, but not yet what changed for the business because of you.
reviewers.decision_question: Would this person move something the business cares about, and in a year would I fight to keep them?

reviewers.name: Future Teammate
reviewers.one_line_take: I could hand you an Excel task next sprint; SQL and dashboards would need some ramp-up.
reviewers.decision_question: Would I want this person on my team for next week's work, and could they contribute without a lot of hand-holding?

reviewers.name: Skeptic
reviewers.one_line_take: The 300% sales line will not survive one follow-up question; the rest holds up.
reviewers.decision_question: Which lines would not survive a five-minute probe in an interview or a reference check, and does anything read as inflated even if it is true?

closest_to_reject.reason: A 300% sales claim with no baseline or method

issues.title: SQL is required but only shows up as a class

evidence.quote: Experience with SQL and Microsoft Excel

issues.detail: The posting asks for SQL experience. I see it in your coursework and skills list, but no line shows you using it, so I cannot tell how far you got.

fixes.suggestion: If a class project used SQL, describe it in one line with what you queried.
fixes.candidate_question: What did you do with SQL in your class projects?

issues.title: Internship bullets describe duties, not results

evidence.quote: Responsible for the weekly email newsletter to about 600 subscribers
Helped with Instagram posts 3x a week

issues.detail: I can see what you were responsible for, not what changed because you did it.

fixes.suggestion: Say what you wrote or tracked and what happened next.
fixes.candidate_question: What happened because of the newsletter or the posts you tracked?

fixes.suggestion: Say what you made or tracked, using your real level of involvement.
Add what happened because of the newsletter, if you know it.
fixes.candidate_question: Did the newsletter or the tracked posts change anything the store did?

issues.title: The top third reads marketing, not analytics
issues.detail: In a fast skim I see Marketing Intern and newsletter work first. The analytics side of you shows up later.

fixes.suggestion: Open the internship with the sales numbers bullet so analytics shows in the first lines.
Keep the real title. Lead the bullets with the data work you did, like the weekly sales numbers.

issues.title: Your closest match to this job sits low on the page

evidence.quote: Designed a 12 question survey with 3 classmates and collected 140 responses

issues.detail: The survey project is the most analytics-heavy thing here and it comes after two jobs.

fixes.suggestion: Move the survey project up, or lead the internship with the sales numbers work.
Put the survey project right after Education.

issues.title: A 300% sales claim with no baseline or method

evidence.quote: Increased online sales by 300% during the summer sale

issues.detail: 300% compared to what, over what period, and what was your part? An interviewer will ask, and a vague answer hurts every other line.

fixes.suggestion: Say what you actually did for the sale, and keep the number only with its real baseline.
fixes.candidate_question: What was the 300% measured against, and what did you do for the summer sale?

issues.title: Required job terms are missing from your resume

evidence.quote: - Strong written and verbal communication skills

issues.detail: Recruiters search and filter by the posting's terms, and AI graders check each basic qualification against your resume.

fixes.suggestion: For each missing term you truly have, show it in a bullet about real work. If you don't have it, leave it out.
fixes.candidate_question: Where have you shown communication: a job, class, club or volunteering?

fixes.suggestion: Show communication through real work you already did, such as the newsletter or the pricing presentation.
fixes.candidate_question: Did you write the newsletter yourself, and who did you present the survey results to?

issues.title: Some job terms are only listed, not shown in your experience

evidence.quote: - Experience with SQL and Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP)
- Experience with email marketing tools such as Mailchimp
"SQL" appears only in a list, not in a bullet about your work.

issues.detail: A skill in a list is weaker evidence than a bullet that shows you using it.

fixes.suggestion: Where it is true, mention the skill in a bullet that describes the work you did with it.
fixes.candidate_question: Where have you used SQL, VLOOKUP or Mailchimp? A class, job, project or club counts.

issues.title: Your own part in the team survey is unclear

evidence.quote: Designed a 12 question survey with 3 classmates

issues.detail: The survey is your strongest proof for this job, and it was a team of 4. Which part was yours?

fixes.suggestion: Name the part you did yourself.
fixes.candidate_question: Which part of the bike share survey did you do yourself?

issues.title: Weak openers slow the skim

evidence.quote: Responsible for the weekly email newsletter

issues.detail: Starting bullets with 'Responsible for' and 'Helped with' hides the action.

fixes.suggestion: Start each bullet with what you did, keeping your real level of ownership.

conflicts.claim: • Designed a 12 question survey with 3 classmates and collected 140 responses

sides.view: Strength: A real survey project with a pricing recommendation
Strength: A real survey with 140 responses and a recommendation
Weakness: Your own part in the team survey is unclear
sides.quote: Designed a 12 question survey with 3 classmates

conflicts.which_matters: Praise can get you the interview; in the interview the Skeptic's and Hiring Manager's questions decide. Keep the line only if you can back it up.
